title: Regional hysteresis & capacity-aware routing policy for graceful multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Qureshi
description: Implement a new multi-region routing policy that uses latency hysteresis + capacity headroom signals to avoid flapping, reduce cross-region latency regressions, and enable graceful load shedding and circuit breaking during regional overloads. This ticket covers design, prototype, and an initial rollout plan for the policy in the control plane and routing lib.
acceptance_criteria: 1) P95 tail latency for cross-region failovers does not regresses more than 15% versus baseline for synthetic traffic across 3+ regions.
2) Automatic shedding triggers and circuit-breaker trips are observable in Console with clear reason codes and per-customer percent of shed traffic.
3) No routing churn: region change rate per request stream < 0.1% after hysteresis applied under steady-state noise.
4) Rollout can be toggled per-tenant via Console and has safe kill-switch via feature-flag.
5) Load tests demonstrate stable behavior when a region loses 40% of its capacity for 10 minutes.
6) Unit and integration tests for decision logic and metrics instrumentation land in PR + CI green.
7) Documentation and runbook published with failback and postmortem checklist.
8) Dashboards surface the three core signals used by policy: p95 latency, capacity headroom (tokens/s), and queue length.
decisions: Use hysteresis window (40s) + exponential backoff for repeated geo-pin changes to prevent oscillation.
Combine three signals for steering: observed p95 latency (region), capacity headroom (effective tokens/s), and queue depth. All signals are normalized to a 0..1 steer-score.
Soft geo-pinning: prefer home-region by adding +0.1 bias to its steer-score; only override when remote region steer-score exceeds home-region by threshold 0.25 for > hysteresis window.
Circuit breaker trip condition: (error_rate > 5% OR p95_latency > 2x SLO) AND capacity_headroom < 10% for sustained 30s. Cooling period 60s with linear recovery checks.
Load shedding policy: prioritize shedding non-interactive lower-priority routes first (embedding batch, async jobs) and ensure fair shedding across tenants using proportional quotas.
Expose observability tags: reason_code, source_signal_values, and last_change_timestamp for every routed request in traces.
Rollout strategy: start with internal tenants, then opt-in external tenants, increase to global by region in waves with metric guards.
No hard-dependency on a specific metrics provider; metric selectors abstracted so we can swap metrics backend without changing policy code.
Keep initial policy in control plane with a library shim used by local proxies so behavior is consistent across Dedicated/Private deployments.
Require security review before enabling per-tenant telemetry for non-prod PIIs (marked as false for now).
design_notes: Rationale: existing steering logic is reactive and oscillates under symmetric noise. Hysteresis + normalized capacity signals reduce mean regraft rate and lower tail latencies during failover.
Signal normalization: use z-score with per-region rolling window (10m) to smooth spikes, then clamp to [0,1]. This avoids overweighting transient jitter.
Headroom calc: effective_tokens_per_sec = provisioned_tokens * (1 - current_utilization). We will add a slow-moving EWMA for utilization with alpha=0.2.
Backpressure: add per-stream circuit tokens to avoid overfilling internal queues; when queue depth > Q_high (configurable per model-size), immediately triage to shed policy.
Throttles & fairness: implement tenant-weighted shedding where each tenant has an adjustable weight; weights default to usage-based percentiles.
Testing harness: extend chaos tests to simulate partial region loss (packet loss, CPU cap) and verify policy meets acceptance criteria.
Migration: preserve current steering as fallback; rollout will allow 'policy=v1|v2' selector to revert instantly.
Console: add per-tenant routing preview and dry-run mode to see where traffic would go without changing traffic.
Metrics: add new Grafana panels for steering_decisions/sec, region_switches/min, shed_rate_by_tenant, and cb_trips_by_region.
Instrumentation: add proto fields to request traces: routed_region, candidate_scores, and chosen_reason_code.
Estimate basis: 5 dev-weeks for control-plane + routing lib work, 2 weeks for integration and rollout automation, 1 week buffer for docs and runbook.
Alternatives considered: strict geo-pin (too brittle), purely latency-only routing (ignores capacity leading to overload), and centralized queue (operationally heavy).
implementation_todo: 1) API: add new routing policy config schema and feature-flag toggle (platform-api).
2) Routing lib: implement steer-score computation, hysteresis timers, and decision exporter (routing-lib).
3) Control plane: expose per-tenant overrides and dry-run preview endpoints in Console (console-backend + frontend work).
4) Observability: add metrics and tracing fields; create Grafana panels and alert rules (ops-dashboard).
5) Testing: extend e2e chaos suite to simulate region degradation and run load tests (k6 + internal harness).
6) Docs & Runbook: write failover playbook, troubleshooting steps, and postmortem guidelines.
7) Rollout plan: internal -> selected tenants -> global, gated by metric guards and manual approval.
8) PRs: land prototype PR, follow-up integration PR, and feature-flagging PRs for Console toggles.
